editorial_standard: One distinct reader decision per core pattern. Use concise visual-led articles: a brief problem and principle, a main controlled demonstration, shorter variations, practical uses, meaningful limits, explained neighbors and sources. Preserve accessible alternatives, comparison access and necessary qualifications; retain complete prior wording and production detail in editorial records. Length follows complexity rather than a fixed quota.
metadata_mapping: The groups list is the planned inventory, not a list of completed articles. Only drafted articles appear under patterns and in canonical collections. Rich authoring metadata stays here; canonical frontmatter follows the existing schema. Recommendation queries do not imply a new service.

patterns.title: Define the Core Message

patterns.title: Crop for Impact
patterns.short_description: Adjust the visible window within an image to emphasize useful content, protect important outlines and retain necessary context, while keeping the framing truthful to its purpose.

A fixed crop clips a product feature that exists in the source.
A close crop omits the context needed to understand an offer.

Distinguish tightening, equal-scale shifting and widening.
Preserve important outlines, context and truthful representation.
mechanisms: fitting a smaller source window enlarges retained content inside a fixed frame
shifting an equal-size window exchanges peripheral content without zoom
widening can restore a relationship or feature
crop boundaries determine which meaningful outlines survive
aspect-ratio matching preserves geometry while output requirements limit useful magnification
prerequisites: The uncropped source and a clear communication purpose.

not_ideal_when: The source never contained the needed feature.

patterns.title: Integrate Text and Image
patterns.short_description: Coordinate the meaning, placement and connections of words and pictures so viewers can understand what belongs together while each remains useful and readable.
use_when: Relevant pictures and offer details are separated by unrelated material.
Feature names need an explicit connection to locations in an image.
Readable lettering covers the part of a photograph that contributes necessary meaning.
goals: Coordinate complementary information across words and pictures.
Make caption and label referents clear.
Preserve both image content and text readability at delivered sizes.
mechanisms: adjacent offers reduce the distance between a photograph and corresponding practical details
leader endpoints disambiguate exact feature locations
coordinated text placement preserves the visual contribution of a subject
wording identifies what the image alone cannot establish
responsive grouping and text alternatives preserve relationships across delivery modes
prerequisites: Relevant imagery and an identified communication purpose.

not_ideal_when: The selected source is irrelevant or implies the wrong relationship.
The brief intentionally separates image experience from reference details.
Labels require more detail than the image can show at the intended size.

patterns.title: Simplify Through Abstraction
patterns.short_description: Replace incidental appearance with selected shapes, relationships or steps that preserve the information needed for a particular recognition or understanding task.
use_when: A category cue is tied to the material appearance of one specimen.
Perspective and decor obscure a conceptual arrangement summary.
A photograph shows materials but not the relationships in a written procedure.
goals: Select the features or relationships required by the communication task.
Change representation without inventing precision or unsupported information.
Explain what is lost and when the detailed source remains preferable.
mechanisms: defining feature combinations preserve category recognition while surface appearance is omitted
a conceptual overhead model replaces perspective with selected spatial relationships
schematic symbols and arrows encode a known procedure
labels and external text make the intended model explicit
purpose determines which details can be omitted and which must survive
prerequisites: A defined recognition or understanding task.
A trustworthy brief specifying relationships that must survive.
not_ideal_when: Readers must inspect real materials, exact dimensions, state or evidence.
Simplification deletes the feature that distinguishes the subject.
Clean geometry would imply unsupported precision.

patterns.title: Use Visual Metaphors
patterns.short_description: Borrow a recognizable quality or relationship from one subject to communicate another, making the intended comparison clear and checking the implications it brings with it.
use_when: Literal topic imagery does not show the relationship the campaign wants to propose.
A coherent metaphor image leaves the intended subject ambiguous.
An attractive comparison imports implications that conflict with the brief.
goals: Specify the subject, borrowed source and intended transferred relationship.
Use visual conjunction or explanatory wording to make the comparison interpretable.
Review unwanted properties and alternatives before committing to a metaphor.
mechanisms: conjoining a book and seedling visually proposes a growth relationship
explicit wording identifies a target for an unchanged visual source
source selection changes which relational structure is available to transfer
audience knowledge and message familiarity influence interpretation
keeping practical facts explicit limits dependence on metaphor decoding
prerequisites: A clear communication claim and intended audience.

not_ideal_when: The brief needs literal evidence, measured diagrams or precise instructions.
Shared background knowledge cannot be assumed for a necessary message.

patterns.title: Employ Recognizable Symbols
patterns.short_description: Use visual signs whose meanings the intended audience can already recognize, match them to the actual service or action, and add words where the meaning remains uncertain.

A familiar icon contradicts the action or label it accompanies.
People recognize an object but cannot infer the service behind it.
goals: Select a convention suited to the actual audience and medium.
Keep the selected symbol semantically consistent with its service or action.
Retain visible words for meanings the symbol cannot communicate precisely.
mechanisms: learned associations offer a candidate meaning before all wording is read
agreement among symbol, label and context supports one interpretation
visible wording disambiguates services represented by the same familiar object
recognizability and interpretation require separate evaluation
prerequisites: A defined audience, service or action and intended medium.
Access to conventions used in that audience’s context.
not_ideal_when: A symbol would require as much explanation as the complete text label.
The brief needs a novel conceptual comparison rather than an established cue.
A precise service or specification cannot be represented by the familiar sign alone.

patterns.title: Establish a Shared Visual Language
patterns.short_description: Define dependable visual roles across related artifacts, deciding which features stay consistent and which may vary with content, format and use.
use_when: Related materials look individually considered but their roles drift across formats.
A repeated motif appears to signify different things in different places.
Compulsory sameness prevents an image or format from serving its content.
goals: Define stable roles and allowed variation across related artifacts.
Make repeated motifs serve a clear bounded job.
Keep format/content adaptations compatible with the shared rules.
mechanisms: recurring treatments can carry expectations across encounters
a bounded motif role limits unintended changes in apparent meaning
separating a content slot from its selected value permits purposeful variation
explicit exceptions and ownership keep the agreement maintainable
prerequisites: A set of related artifacts and known tasks for each.
A reason for these materials to share an identity.
not_ideal_when: The materials need independent identities or commissions.
The main problem is confusion with another organization rather than internal coherence.
Required language or accessibility adaptations are being suppressed by style rules.
example_user_queries: Our poster, ticket and reminder look like they came from different organizations.
We use the same fonts but their jobs change from one format to another.
How can these materials belong together without using the exact same layout?
Our brand motif appears everywhere but nobody knows what it means.

related_patterns.relationship: Repairs a particular appearance-to-meaning mapping; shared language coordinates those roles across artifacts.
Coordinates recurrence and pauses within a sequence; repeating an identity cue across documents does not by itself create rhythm.
Addresses source recognition among external alternatives rather than internal consistency alone.
Makes a suitable form and shared visual roles repeatable with changing content.

visual_decision.reason: Three cross-artifact sets isolate stable type roles, bounded repetition and activity-specific image variation. Typography/layout are native; photographic sources reused. Narrow views interleave each artifact’s before and after for inspection.

sources.supports: GOV.UK principle9 recommends consistent language/patterns with flexibility for circumstances and changing user needs. Design guidance, not a test of these materials.

patterns.title: Develop Distinctive Visual Cues
patterns.short_description: Select and repeat identity features that remain distinguishable among relevant alternatives, survive their viewing conditions and build a dependable association with their source.
use_when: An internally coherent identity resembles nearby providers in real listings.
A distinguishing feature disappears at thumbnail or small-print size.
A candidate identity cue could imply an unsupported function or promise.
goals: Develop identity candidates against a relevant comparison set.
Preserve identifying features through required reproduction sizes.
Evaluate source attribution without mistaking novelty for recognition.
mechanisms: a stable cue paired with a name offers opportunities to learn their association
similar cues can fit more than one source in the comparison set
fine detail cannot contribute where reproduction fails to preserve it
identity cues can introduce unintended service interpretations
prerequisites: An intended audience and actual viewing contexts.
Relevant alternatives and existing identity associations to examine.
not_ideal_when: The reader needs a conventional functional symbol rather than an identity cue.
A familiar asset is being discarded solely for stylistic novelty.
The main failure is inconsistent production within one identity.
example_user_queries: Our event cards look just like the other providers in the directory.
People recognize the style but confuse us with another organization.
How can I tell whether a new logo is distinctive or just unfamiliar?
Our mark looks good large but disappears in email headers.

related_patterns.relationship: Coordinates stable roles across related materials; distinctive cues address confusion with external alternatives.
Uses shared conventions for meaning or function; identity cues depend on association with a particular source.
Preserves task-relevant information while removing detail; can repair a small-size cue without proving distinctiveness.
Makes a suitable form and shared visual roles repeatable with changing content.

visual_decision.reason: Three photo-led native comparisons isolate selected identity artwork in an external listing, small-size production proof and possible service-association case. All unrelated artwork variables remain fixed.

sources.supports: Jenni Romaniuk distinguishes fame (association with the brand) and uniqueness (association with that brand rather than alternatives). This supports evaluating learned attribution instead of treating novelty as proof.

patterns.title: Build Reusable Templates
patterns.short_description: Define editable content roles, required information and tested layout responses so recurring materials can accept new inputs without reconstructing the design or losing meaning.
use_when: Recurring notices require layout repairs whenever supplied text changes.
A condition or qualification is separated from the offer it explains.
Missing inputs cause old imagery or values to survive into a new edition.
goals: Reuse content roles and layout responses rather than merely duplicating a file.
Preserve necessary information across different supplied inputs.
Make safe changes and review conditions clear to the next editor.
mechanisms: named roles and required inputs preserve the content obligations of a recurring artifact
defined flow responds to title length without changing type size
conditional grouping keeps eligibility beside its price
explicit absence variants avoid inheriting stale imagery or data
filled difficult inputs reveal capacity and fallback problems before handoff
prerequisites: A genuinely recurring communication task and suitable format.
Representative inputs, including longer, conditional and absent content.
not_ideal_when: A one-off commission does not justify maintaining reusable rules.
The recurring format itself is unsuitable for the intended task.
Exceptions dominate and the template scope needs reconsideration.
example_user_queries: We copy last month’s design and have to repair the layout every time.
A longer event title makes important details disappear.
How do we keep a discount condition next to its price in every edition?
Our template still shows last month’s photograph when no new image arrives.
The layout looks good with sample text but fails with real content.
People keep shrinking type to fit a fixed box.
How can another editor safely change the design without losing information?
Our monthly report needs an extra data note and there is nowhere to put it.
Which parts of a recurring design should be fixed and which should adapt?
When do we need another approved layout instead of another workaround?

related_patterns.relationship: Defines stable visual roles and permitted variation; templates carry those roles into recurring production.
Provides geometry; a template also defines content obligations and responses to varying inputs.
Establishes that the format serves the task before reuse is worth preserving.
Prepares readable phrases within the text area without replacing capacity and overflow rules.

visual_decision.reason: Three data-driven renderer comparisons each use two filled inputs: short/long title, standard/conditional offer and photo/absent-image review with longer note. Ordinary inputs remain unchanged controls. Only declared viewport, flow, optional-image and card-height properties change.

sources.supports: Adobe documents reusable parent pages and inheritance of repeated elements. This supports one production mechanism, not the editorial content obligations proposed here.

GOV.UK recommends testing prototypes and distinguishes prototype code from production-ready implementations. The article applies this distinction to template trials and handoff.

retired_patterns.title: Use Scale to Establish Importance
retired_patterns.short_description: Make relative sizes express what the viewer needs first, while keeping supporting information readable.
use_when: The viewer cannot tell what matters first.
Decoration dominates the intended message.
Several report values compete without a clear editorial focus.
goals: Align visible prominence with the audience’s immediate communication needs.
Keep supporting information readable.
prerequisites: A stated communication goal and content to arrange.
not_ideal_when: Elements need equal status for fair comparison.
An oversized heading would obstruct the intended task.
example_user_queries: Everything on my poster seems equally important.
People notice my logo but miss what the event is about.
How can I make the main message stand out without adding more colors?
My report has several big numbers and no clear takeaway.
The headline looks large in the editor but disappears in the phone preview.
How do I make the date easy to find after people notice the event?
My design feels like several headlines competing with each other.
How can I reduce the decoration without losing the design’s character?

related_patterns.relationship: Chooses the intended takeaway before scale makes its priority visible.
Includes differences in value, pattern and type, alongside relative size.
Assigns the content roles and repeated levels that relative size can express.
Chooses a useful center of attention; relative size is one means of establishing it.

visual_decision.reason: Finished photo-led print designs reuse identical local photographic image bytes, crops, paper and lighting. Authored typography and the workshop rosette change only in scale, with fixed positions and weights.

sources.supports: Scale as relative size and one mechanism within visual hierarchy.
Noticeable size differences and audience-dependent importance.

retired_patterns.title: Establish a Focal Point
retired_patterns.short_description: Give a meaningful element or group a distinct leading role so the composition offers a useful place to begin.
use_when: Several elements share the strongest treatment despite an intended lead.
A pricing or other practical unit needs a local visual anchor.
Repeated primary treatments leave an action group without a leading role.
goals: Choose a content-bearing anchor suited to the encounter.
Distinguish the anchor without removing access to supporting detail.
Evaluate local focus and competing emphasis rather than assuming a guaranteed first fixation.
mechanisms: spatial isolation of an intact group
prerequisites: A clear communication purpose and a reason for the chosen element to lead.
not_ideal_when: Equal-status information should remain comparable.
Exploratory or reference use benefits from distributed attention.
The proposed anchor is irrelevant or misleading for the actual task.
example_user_queries: Everything on the poster seems equally important.
Where should someone start looking at this layout?
The event title competes with all its supporting attractions.
Can I give something emphasis without making it bigger?
The price is readable but it gets lost in the specification list.
How can white space help a practical detail stand out?
Every button looks like the main action.
Can I make the main action clearer by quieting the others?
Does every design need one dominant element?
My decorative badge gets more attention than the message.
How do I keep qualifications attached to a prominent price?

related_patterns.relationship: Chooses what a piece should establish; a focal point gives a meaningful part of that intention a visible leading role.
Supplies one means of prominence; focal points can also use weight, isolation or reduced competition.
Uses purposeful differences to establish an anchor, while contrast also distinguishes peer categories and roles.
Aligns cues around a focal point with useful destinations.

visual_decision.reason: Three controlled comparisons change only one headline weight, a pricing-group horizontal translation, or secondary-action paints. No font sizes change, and unrelated artwork and presentation remain fixed.

sources.supports: Relative emphasis and audience-dependent priority; applications through weight and isolation are editorial interpretation.
Multiple influences on attentional guidance; no guarantee of first fixation for these fictional layouts.
Distinguish main and secondary actions; avoid multiple default buttons. The custom outlined treatment is original.
Preserve meaning through visible cues beyond hue where color conveys information or prompts action.

retired_patterns.title: Create Deliberate Contrast
retired_patterns.short_description: Use a visible difference in a chosen attribute to clarify a meaningful distinction, while keeping unrelated elements consistent.
use_when: Practical text barely separates from its background.
Similar category treatments make matching or tracing difficult.
Different voices or roles need a consistent visual distinction.
goals: Give each visible difference a meaningful job.
Choose a suitable attribute rather than changing everything.
Preserve equal status where distinction does not imply hierarchy.
prerequisites: A defined distinction that matters to the reader.
not_ideal_when: Equal treatments correctly express equal roles.
Extra differences would create an unexplained visual code.
A different attribute conflicts with a stable convention or reproduction constraint.

related_patterns.relationship: Changes light-dark relationships when diagnostic inspection reveals insufficient tonal separation.
Gives colors dependable meanings, which still need another carrier when hue is unavailable.

Repairs isolate four text fills, six direct identifiers or one underline; all unrelated typography, geometry, photo sources/crops and presentation remain fixed. sources.supports: Black & White conversion is adjustable by color; keeping conversion settings fixed matters for controlled comparison.

Text/background contrast calculations complement inspection and have defined thresholds and exceptions.

The Filter Effects working draft documents SVG color matrices and linearRGB filter operations; implementation, not color-vision or printer simulation.

retired_patterns.title: Control the Background
retired_patterns.short_description: Adjust the detail, tone or opacity of the layer behind important content so it supports the communication without hiding necessary context.
use_when: Photographic edges interfere with lettering despite useful subject matter.
Decorative texture competes with a product contour or handle opening.
A translucent information card transmits changing image detail.
goals: Target the supporting layer rather than unnecessarily changing foreground content.
Choose between local protection, pattern attenuation and an opaque information surface.
Preserve useful photographic context and acknowledge what treatment conceals.
mechanisms: local opaque backing removes photographic variation immediately behind text
lower pattern opacity reduces decorative edge contrast while preserving geometry
opaque surfaces decouple the effective ground from underlying image content
treatment extent determines which context stays visible
foreground contrast must be checked against the delivered local background
prerequisites: A defined foreground communication task.
Access to the background layer or a source image suited to the layout.
not_ideal_when: Surrounding detail supplies evidence or context needed to understand the subject.
The source image contributes the wrong meaning.
Many local patches are compensating for an unsuitable overall layout.
example_user_queries: The date gets lost against the furniture in my photograph.
Can I keep the image without making the lettering larger?
The product outline is clear but the brand pattern feels too busy.
The pattern through the handle distracts from the object.

Will blurring the image actually improve the text contrast?

How much of the image should a text backing cover?
The cleaner background hides context the reader needs.

related_patterns.relationship: Describes foreground/background perception; controlling the supporting layer is one intervention that can strengthen separation.
Adjusts light-dark differences; background control also addresses detail, transparency and treatment extent.
Changes the visible source window; background treatments address interference remaining inside it.
Selects the source for its contribution; a quiet backdrop cannot make irrelevant imagery meaningful.

visual_decision.reason: Three background-only opacity changes: add a local opaque text backing, attenuate decorative waves behind an identical product cutout, and make a booking information surface opaque. Existing generated assets and all foreground typography/copy/geometry/crops/presentation remain fixed.

sources.supports: Image features can interfere with foreground letter shapes; check local image contrast behind letters.
Rosenholtz, Li and Nakano (2007) investigate visual clutter measures and their relationship to search performance in complex imagery; not a test of these designs.
Treating the area immediately behind text can maintain sufficient local text/background contrast.
Minimum text contrast thresholds and defined exceptions; a limited color-pair check does not establish complete conformance.

retired_patterns.title: Use Silhouettes
retired_patterns.short_description: Use a solid-toned figure to emphasize a subject’s contour and meaningful openings when those shapes can carry the message without internal detail.
use_when: Surface finish is irrelevant to a category cue but dominates its photograph.
A silhouette has useful contour and gaps but weak separation from its ground.
A flat figure needs review because the brief requires interior detail.
goals: Use contour and negative spaces deliberately when they carry the message.
Preserve the same source geometry while removing internal RGB information.
Recognize when another representation is more appropriate.
mechanisms: constant-tone interiors suppress material and lighting cues while retaining source alpha
transparent openings retain meaningful shape structure
background contrast makes outside and inside boundaries more distinct
viewpoint affects which parts remain distinguishable after detail removal
restoring internal detail repairs briefs that exceed silhouette information
prerequisites: A defined image contribution and a suitable source view.
A clean figure boundary and meaningful transparent gaps.
not_ideal_when: The brief requires facial features, material condition or mechanisms.
The selected view merges important parts.
Similar objects differ mainly inside the boundary.
example_user_queries: The category sign looks like it accepts only one product finish.

Should I change the silhouette or the surface behind it?

related_patterns.relationship: Broader reduction can preserve internal lines, change viewpoint or encode processes; silhouettes prioritize filled contour and openings.
Establishes perceptual subject/background distinction on which a silhouette strongly depends.
Repairs silhouette separation by treating its supporting layer without changing shape.
Determines whether the image needs internal detail or can contribute through shape alone.

visual_decision.reason: Three controlled decisions: flatten an unchanged pitcher cutout while preserving its handle opening; change only the ground behind a fixed open-shears silhouette; restore photographic detail to the same maker cutout when the portrait brief requires it. sources.supports: Wagemans et al. (2008) found substantial variation in identifiability of silhouette/outline object versions; recognizability should not be assumed.

foundations.title: Contrast as a Foundation
foundations.short_description: Choose the kind of visible difference needed for legibility, category distinction or hierarchy, then use the appropriate design intervention.

completed_core_briefs.title: Establish a Shared Visual Language
completed_core_briefs.decision: Define what remains invariant across artifacts and where content-specific variation is allowed.
completed_core_briefs.failure: A programme, ticket and reminder all use different treatments for the same roles, or their sameness prevents necessary format adaptation.
completed_core_briefs.intervention: Specify a small vocabulary of type, color, graphic and content roles with explicit variation rules.
example_briefs: Unify the roles of event title, date and booking action across a poster, ticket and email while retaining different layouts.
Repeat a limited motif with a stable function; remove unrelated repetition that is merely decorative.
Allow the session image and accent to vary while keeping practical information and functional cues dependable.
completed_core_briefs.boundaries: Cross-artifact coherence and rule ownership. Similarity handles a local role mapping; Rhythm handles recurrence and pace; Distinctive Cues handles confusion with other identities.
completed_core_briefs.evidence_needed: Develop comparisons across multiple related artifacts; do not claim recognition gains without audience evidence.

completed_core_briefs.title: Develop Distinctive Visual Cues
completed_core_briefs.decision: Choose features that help the intended audience distinguish this identity among plausible alternatives.
completed_core_briefs.failure: An internally consistent design is confused with another organization in a realistic surrounding set.
completed_core_briefs.intervention: Select and repeat distinguishing features that survive actual viewing conditions.
example_briefs: Compare two internally coherent but confusable event identities in a shared listing.
Repair a cue that disappears at small size while preserving identity information.
Check whether a new differentiating feature introduces an inappropriate service association.
completed_core_briefs.boundaries: External recognition and discrimination, not internal consistency alone. A recognizable generic information icon is a service convention, not a distinctive identity asset.
completed_core_briefs.evidence_needed: Specify the actual comparison set and audience; test recognition instead of inferring it from novelty.

completed_core_briefs.title: Build Reusable Templates
completed_core_briefs.decision: Provide reusable content roles and production rules for recurring artifacts with variable inputs.
completed_core_briefs.failure: Each edition requires reconstruction or loses necessary content when a title, price condition or image changes.
completed_core_briefs.intervention: Define editable slots, required information, useful defaults and safe exceptions.
example_briefs: Use the same workshop notice template with short and long titles without shrinking essential facts.
Add an eligibility condition and keep it near the offer it qualifies.
Adapt a recurring review to missing imagery and an additional data note without inventing information.
completed_core_briefs.boundaries: Production reuse and content variability. A grid provides geometric regions; a template also specifies content obligations and editing behavior.
completed_core_briefs.evidence_needed: Show multiple realistic content substitutions and resulting artifacts; do not treat a blank wireframe as a finished worked example.
